title: The forest remembers
subtitle: what gets left behind
narrative: The empire ends. The trees do not. Every fantasy setting is built on land somebody used to live on, and the cards know it. A broken golden weapon in the undergrowth. A cityscape pulled apart by jungle. A guildgate at twilight with branches in the masonry. A vine in the shape of a portcullis. Two treefolk walking through ancient forest interior. Thirteen cards. The forest as the slow eater of everything claimed in someone's name. This is not nature aesthetic. This is what survives a war.

cards.name: Asceticism
cards.why_it_fits: Deep forest interior. Canopy high, light filtered green. No figures, no path, no buildings. Just the trees doing what trees do when nobody is watching. The card the bundle is built around.

cards.name: Return to Nature
cards.why_it_fits: A broken golden spear lying on the forest floor, vines climbing the haft. The flavor frames it as the weapon of a god, but the art is the spear and the green eating the spear.

cards.name: Urban Evolution
cards.why_it_fits: A Ravnican cityscape with the buildings still standing but green pulled through every window and over every roof. The jungle is winning. The card name is dry about it.

cards.name: Gruul Guildgate (250)
cards.why_it_fits: A guildgate at twilight, lanterns lit, but with branches and moss already on the masonry. The civic infrastructure is still functional. The forest is patient.

cards.name: Natural Reclamation
cards.why_it_fits: Forest floor under broken stonework, what looks like a column overgrown. The spell does what the name says. The card name is also the bundle title in plain English.

cards.name: New Horizons
cards.why_it_fits: An old tree with its roots exposed in a sunlit chamber under the canopy. The roots are the size of the columns in any of the other ruins in this bundle. The tree was there first.

cards.name: Portcullis Vine
cards.why_it_fits: A heavy vine hung in the shape of an iron portcullis across an arched ruin. The vine does the gate's job now. The card name is the picture.

cards.name: Forest (262)
cards.why_it_fits: The basic Forest from War of the Spark. Ravnican towers half-eaten by green at sunset. A basic land doing a lot of editorial work for a card that just produces green mana.

cards.name: Tuinvale Treefolk
cards.why_it_fits: A walking treefolk, moss-coated, eyes deep in the bark. Two copies in this bundle because we have two copies in inventory.

cards.name: Gnarled Sage
cards.why_it_fits: Another treefolk, this one knotted and ancient, vines wound through the trunk. Three copies because we have three copies in inventory and the bundle benefits from showing the forest's witnesses in numbers.

pricing.diy_alternative_note: Thirteen cards spread across eight sets. Plus the Asceticism uncommon is a $6.79 anchor that ships from its own seller most of the time. Realistic 5-seller floor; could be higher.
pricing.shipping_policy: buyer-paid, itemized separately at checkout; never included in list price
pricing.premium_justification: The Asceticism uncommon carries most of the inventory value. The premium pays for the writing and the arrangement. Thirteen cards in a sequence, one thesis.

metadata.notes: Second sample bundle. Different tier from Tithe ($5 floor, all commons): this is mid-tier with one $6.79 uncommon anchor and meaningful multi-copy leverage (Gnarled Sage x3, Tuinvale Treefolk x2). Pairs both Labor and Rebellion hubs since 'empire ends and the trees remain' is anti-extraction (labor) AND anti-establishment (rebellion). Validates the schema across a different price tier, palette, and tonal register than Tithe.
